Get the default priors for an edge model

Source: R/priors.R
get_default_priors.Rd

Returns the default priors for a type of edge model, as a starting point for choosing priors. A prior describes which values of a parameter are plausible before seeing the data. The defaults may not suit every study, so check them with prior_check() and prior_predictive_check() and change them where needed before passing them to bison_model().

Usage

get_default_priors(model_type)

Arguments

model_type

The type of model: "binary", "count", "binary_conjugate" or "count_conjugate".

Value

A named list of priors, in the format used by the priors argument of bison_model().

Details

Each prior is a string naming a distribution and its parameters, such as "normal(0, 2.5)". The entries are:

  • edge: the edge weights. For "binary" and "count" models this is a normal distribution on the link scale (log-odds for binary models, log rates for count models). With partial_pooling = TRUE, the second value is instead the scale of a half-normal prior on the spread of the edge weights. For "binary_conjugate" it is a beta distribution on the probability, and for "count_conjugate" a gamma distribution (shape, rate) on the rate.

  • fixed: fixed effects, as a normal distribution on the link scale.

  • random_std: the standard deviation of random effects, as a half-normal distribution with the given scale.

  • zero_prob: in zero-inflated models, the probability that a row of data is a structural zero (a zero regardless of the edge weight), as a beta distribution.

Conjugate models only have an edge prior. Priors for terms that a model doesn't include, such as fixed in a model without fixed effects, have no effect.

See also

prior_check(), prior_predictive_check(), bison_model()

Examples

priors <- get_default_priors("binary")
priors
#> $edge
#> [1] "normal(0, 2.5)"
#> 
#> $fixed
#> [1] "normal(0, 2.5)"
#> 
#> $random_std
#> [1] "half-normal(1)"
#> 
#> $zero_prob
#> [1] "beta(1, 1)"
#> 
# Priors are strings describing distributions, and can be changed:
priors$edge <- "normal(-1, 1.5)"
